newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PolyDoc to float in Amsterdam on March 25.
newsitem.headline: PolyDoc to float in Amsterdam on March 25.

text.p: Information software firm PolyDoc Plc will be listed on the Amsterdam bourse from March 25, lead manager Rabo Securities said on Wednesday.

Dutch-based PolyDoc will be the first firm to be listed on the New Market Amsterdam (NMAX) of the Amsterdam Exchanges, a new trading segment for young and fast growing companies with international ambitions.
"The purpose of this listing on the NMAX is to broaden PolyDoc's investor base, and establish its name recognition further," Rabo Securities said.
A maximum of 528.000 already existing ordinary shares in PolyDoc Plc will be offered until March 24, 1400 GMT, through a book-building system. No new shares will be issued.
PolyDoc's shares were listed on London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in September 1996 when about 4.5 million shares were floated.
Dutch venture capital firm Nederlandse Participatie Maatschappij (NPM) said in January it had taken up about one third of that offering which gave it an 8.15 percent stake in PolyDoc.
PolyDoc was set up in 1993 by British entrepreneur Barry Mence.
At the time of its London flotation, the firm said it would reach a break-even in 1996 but in a letter to shareholders last December Mence said this might not be the case.
He said then 1996 would bring an overall loss for PolyDoc if it failed to finalise three orders by the end of the year.

Rabo Securities' spokesman Huub Maas told Reuters that PolyDoc, which has not yet published its results, now expected a 1996 loss of less than 0.5 million stg. But expectations for 1997 and later years were very positive, he added.
In December's letter to shareholders, Mence said he did not consider a possible loss in 1996 to be material in relation to PolyDoc's longer term prospects.
